summary: Buffered single-character write with overflow handling. Takes a character a1 and a stream-buffer control struct a2 (a2[0] is the current byte cursor, a2[1] the remaining-capacity counter). Decrements the capacity counter; if it goes negative the buffer is full and the overflow path sub_58CF35(a1, a2) is taken, otherwise the low byte of a1 is written at the cursor and the cursor advances. The whole operation is wrapped in a critical-section lock/unlock pair. Returns the written byte value on the normal path, or the overflow path's result.

operations.description: Enter the buffer's critical section via StreamBufferLockViaCriticalSection(a2).
Decrement the remaining-capacity counter a2[1] and test whether it fell below zero, detecting buffer overflow.
If a2[1] < 0 the buffer is full: take the overflow path, else write in place.
Overflow path: call sub_58CF35(a1, a2) (flush/reserve handler) and store its result in v3.
Normal path: v3 = (unsigned __int8)a1, then write that byte at the current cursor *a2 and advance the cursor (*a2)++.
Leave the buffer's critical section via AddressRangeCriticalSectionLeave(a2).
Return v3, the written byte value or the overflow path's result.

clean_pseudocode: result = sub_58CF35(ch, buf);  // buffer full: flush/reserve path
*((unsigned char *)*buf)++ = (unsigned char)ch;  // write byte, advance cursor
unresolved: Identity and exact behavior of the overflow handler sub_58CF35 are unknown; whether it flushes buffered bytes to a destination or grows the buffer is unproven.
The layout of the a2 control struct beyond the cursor (a2[0]) and capacity counter (a2[1]) is not evidenced.
What stores the written byte stream and when buffered data is flushed to its final destination is outside this function's evidence.
